meaning: Sphyrna, presumably an accidental or intentional misspelling of sphyraena (minus “ae”), the “hammerfish” dating to Aristotle, referring to the hammer-shaped head; tiburo, from tiburon, Spanish for shark, a name given by 16th- and 17th-century navigators to one or more large species of shark
description: The smallest hammerhead, with a smooth, rounded, shovel-shaped head instead of a wide hammer. It is grey to grey-brown above and lighter below. It forages over shallow seagrass flats and bays, eating mostly crabs and shrimp, and it also swallows and digests seagrass.
eats: Crabs, shrimp, mollusks, small fish and seagrass
